title: Otis's singing and writing Swallows while ill with tuberculosis
summary: Rene recalls Otis's singing, his own tuberculosis and sanitarium stay, and writing in a garage where Swallows came from.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I don't know. Otis might have sung a song or something. I like the way Otis sang. He used to sing. He had a funny kind of a sound. Yeah. He had a lot of drive in his singing. Yeah. Very good sound. Otis sang. Well, it's just... He was good. We wrote together. But I wrote... Because I didn't have him all the time. He was a druggist. Performance. And I didn't... He couldn't write with me all the time. I had nothing else to do. Because I was sick at the time. I had TB. And I had nothing else that I could do but write. Oh, you had it too. Oh, sure. That's what... You went to Sanitarium? That's how I was at Sanitarium. I was up there two years. And I said, when I came back, I said, nothing else I could do. That's why a little garage in the back of my mother-in-law's house is where I did write. That's where Swallows came from. It's quite a long story about Swallows. When the Swallows come back to Capistron. Yeah, because I... That's when I just came... I just was released from theology center too. I came back and I was in the little house in the back where they all helped build it. They gave me a place away from the kids.
